title: Risk level boundary
scenario: A caregiver has overweight/central adiposity and a strong family history of diabetes, but no confirmed diabetes or other established cardiometabolic diagnosis is documented.
task: Ask the learner to assign a SAI SPARSH risk level and explain the deciding factor.
engine: Short case -> decision -> brief reasoning -> graded hint if incorrect -> retry with a variant.
validation: Exact L1/L2/L3 definitions must be confirmed before scoring is locked.

title: Stable disease versus acute/high-risk state
scenario: A caregiver has established cardiometabolic disease that is clinically stable and is already under medical follow-up. Another similar caregiver is in a recent acute/post-procedure phase.
task: Ask the learner whether both belong in the same risk category and why.
engine: Branching case; learner must distinguish stable disease from a situation needing more immediate clinical oversight.
validation: Exact Level 3/4 boundaries and use of S modifier must be confirmed.

title: Low-confidence pledge
scenario: A caregiver proposes a major dietary change but reports low confidence that they can sustain it.
task: Ask the learner how they would respond and what they would do next.
engine: Simulated caregiver dialogue. Reward exploration of barriers and movement toward a smaller, achievable pledge rather than simple encouragement.
validation: Confirm whether the 70%/7-of-10 threshold is a hard rule or a coaching heuristic.

title: Affordability and contextual adaptation
scenario: A caregiver says the suggested 'healthy' foods or oils are too expensive for the household budget.
task: Ask the learner to adapt the recommendation without shaming the caregiver or abandoning the goal.
engine: Conversational practice with at least two possible barriers: cost and household preference.
validation: Use only approved SAI SPARSH dietary guidance and locally appropriate examples.

title: Night-shift exception
scenario: A caregiver works rotating night shifts and says a standard meal-timing recommendation does not fit their work schedule.
task: Ask the learner to avoid mechanically applying a daytime rule and instead explore schedule, sleep, meal access and feasible alternatives.
engine: Branching conversation; poor path = rigid rule; preferred path = contextual exploration and tailored pledge.
validation: Exact approved shift-work guidance should be confirmed before fixed feedback is used.

title: Symptom that exceeds coaching scope
scenario: During a lifestyle-coaching interaction, a caregiver reports a new symptom that could require medical evaluation.
task: Ask the learner whether to continue lifestyle coaching, offer reassurance, or stop and refer/escalate.
engine: Safety case with a critical-error flag if the learner gives medical treatment advice or dismisses the symptom.

title: Medication question
scenario: A caregiver reports a possible medication side effect and asks whether they should stop or change the medicine.
task: Ask the learner to respond while preserving the volunteer's role boundary.
engine: Dialogue exercise; correct path should set the boundary, support the caregiver, and route to the appropriate clinician rather than alter medication.
validation: Specific urgency/timing language requires programme-owner approval.

title: Missing follow-up data
scenario: A caregiver could not be reached and therefore a planned follow-up measure or behaviour status could not be confirmed.
task: Ask the learner how to record the item.
engine: Deterministic documentation exercise; distinguish missing/unknown from 'No' or failure.
validation: Confirm the programme's official missing-data and denominator policy.

title: Partial progress
scenario: A caregiver completed part, but not all, of an agreed behaviour pledge.
task: Ask the learner how to discuss the result and how to document progress.
engine: Short case + coaching response. Reward recognition of progress and exploration of barriers rather than binary failure language.
validation: Confirm official follow-up status categories and documentation rules.
